I will still do what I know works here, and I will not change too much. On my 8 mu, I will keep most land in wheat-maize because that is the steady way to get grain and cash, and with my well I am not afraid to water when the crop is thirsty. I will leave 2 mu for cotton and put 6 mu into the wheat-maize rotation. I usually look first at what I did last year, then I look at fertilizer price and seed price. Fertilizer is expensive, but if I cut too much and the yield drops, that hurts more. So I will keep wheat a bit heavier on fertilizer, maize a little less than wheat but still enough, and cotton in the middle because cotton can make money if the stand is good. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because people around me have seen better yield from those, and for cotton I will also use better seed instead of old saved seed. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it saves labor and fits my size. With 8 mu and some family working off-farm, I will keep the plan simple: enough base fertilizer, 2 to 4 irrigations depending on crop, and pesticides only when needed but I will count on a few sprays because insects and disease never wait for me.
